While the fact is fascinating, the headline is a little misleading. The really interesting problem the article focuses on is the fact that the amount of plastic in the ocean is only a small percentage of the total amount of plastic estimated to be dumped into the ocean--meaning that some of this plastic is missing. I think the notion that animals are eating the plastic is the most plausible possibility and I hope researchers can study this in greater detail. Obviously it's a concern if it gets into the food chain or if it affects birth rates of sea life--but maybe there's some critter out there that eats plastic? That would be awesome.
